page0.text:
I can't leave Sakura alone tonight.
My presence alone won't make her any better, but I want to be able to help right away in case she needs it.

page1.text:
"Sorry, Saber. We're not going out on patrol tonight. I'm worried about Sakura."
"...I understand. I will follow your orders, Master."
"Huh?"

page2.text:
T-that's a surprise.
I was sure Saber would be against it, but she simply accepted what I said without protest.

page3.text:
"Lest you misunderstand, Sakura is not the only person who feels unwell. I know you are tired as well, so you should rest tonight.
Your magical energy has yet to recover fully. Neither you nor Sakura should overexert yourselves."
"...Thanks, Saber."

page4.text:
"I-I do not require your gratitude. I am your Servant, Shirou. Your safety comes first of all."
With that, Saber sits down in the living room and pours herself a cup of warm water.

page5.text:
"So, Shirou...what will you do to reward such an understanding attendant?"
Saber asks me a question, her tone adorably mixed with petulance and anticipation.

page6.text:
"Ah. Hang on, Saber."
I divine her desire for a midnight snack, and assemble a tray of tea and cookies that Fuji-nee bought just for her, grinning wryly all the while.

page7.text:
...
My Magic Circuit closes.
Once the red-hot rod leaves my spine, I sigh in relief.

page8.text:
My daily routine, which I've been neglecting lately, goes off without a hitch, to my surprise.
Maybe it's thanks to my contract with Saber. I've always had a hard time forming my Magic Circuit, but it's easy now.

page9.text:
"Still...it isn't of much use if it takes me a whole minute to do it."
All I can do is Strengthen something into a weapon.
If I'm taken by surprise, I'd still be in desperate straits with no way to defend myself.
If I could at least shorten it by half, to about thirty seconds...

page10.text:
"Maybe I'll ask Tohsaka for advice next time. I bet she knows a more efficient way to create a Magic Circuit."
I don't know what she'll want in return though, so I can't just ask her on a moment's notice.

page11.text:
"Hm?"
I hear footsteps on dirt.
They're slow and unhurried.
...It's midnight.
The person who comes to the shed, letting the moonlight guide her path, is...
"Senpai...? Are you still awake?"
Sakura. The color of her face looks a little better.

page12.text:
...
But my mind goes blank.
...Sakura's wearing something I haven't seen before.
I take incomprehensible damage.
They're clothes that Fuji-nee gave her, but seeing Sakura out of her school uniform sends my head spinning...

page13.text:
"Um, Senpai?"
"Uh, yeah. I'm awake. Are you sure you should be up? It's cold outside."
"Yes, my fever is better now. I went out for a walk to clear my head, and I heard some sounds that I thought were you."

page14.text:
"Ah. Well, make sure you warm yourself up and get some sleep later. Glad to see you're feeling better."
I light the stove I just fixed.

page15.text:
Good, it turns on.
It'll warm us up a little.

page16.text:
"Come on over. It's cold here too, but still better than outside.
...If you want someone to talk to before you go back to bed, I'm here for you."
"Okay. If you don't mind."

page17.text:
Sakura makes her way towards me with sure steps.
...I'm glad. She really does look like she's feeling better.

page18.text:
"It's warm. You really fixed this?"
"Somehow. It was so worn out when I first worked on it that I just about gave up."

page19.text:
"I remember you got mad. 'This is like asking me to fix the VCR that Fuji-nee cut in half!'
But you still brought it home in the end."

page20.text:
"...Well, this piece of junk isn't the only one who doesn't know when to give up."
The stove was broken, but once I saw that it could be fixed, I just couldn't leave it alone.

page21.text:
"That's because you're persistent, Senpai. You're a sympathetic person and you're incredibly stubborn. Do you realize that now?"
"...Mrgh. I'm stubborn, huh?"

page22.text:
"You are! And pushy, too.
Even just earlier, you weren't listening to me at all."

page23.text:
Well then.
Sakura's in an oddly good mood, even though she's scolding me.
...Not that I'm unhappy to see her in good spirits again.

page24.text:
"...Sorry. I got a little intense back there, so I wasn't thinking straight."
"That's right. You looked really scary when you were upset at both me and yourself... I know I'm always being a burden on you, but I hope you realize that you were out of line earlier."

page25.text:
"..."
Sakura is so gentle.
She's still getting over her illness, but, how do I put it, it isn't the usual Sakura that's trying to do her best in front of me. It's like I'm seeing the real Sakura.

page26.text:
"It reminded me a little of my childhood.
I was always shut in at home when I was younger, and I could never say the things I wanted to say. I thought that it would be better for everyone else if I kept my true feelings to myself, so I never said anything."

page27.text: "...But I know that can't work. I kept quiet because I didn't want to make anyone worry, but that only made my father and brother worry even more."

page28.text: "...Huh. But you only did it because you care about your dad and Shinji, so I'm sure your feelings got through to them. Not everything needs to be said out loud."

page29.text:
"I hope you're right.
...What about you, Senpai? You've never spoken much about your childhood."

page30.text:
"Oh, me? Hmm...it wasn't really any different from my life now. I ran around town during the day, cooked for my old man, and fixed junk in here at night."
Feeling bashful, I scratch my cheek.
...It's a little embarrassing as a man to admit that my life hasn't changed since childhood.

page31.text:
"Wow. You had to run around town?"
"Mm... I was playing patrol. I always wanted to be someone strong who helps the weak."

page32.text:
My main battlefield was the park.
I recall spending a lot of time there with other kids my age, picking fights with slightly older kids.
...I vaguely recall one of the kids who was really clever for their age, whom I saw as a devilish nemesis.

page33.text:
"I see. You protected the town from bullies. So that's the kind of person you've always been."
"Sakura, when you say that with a smile, it just makes me regret everything I've ever done. You're embarrassing me."

page34.text:
"It's nothing to be ashamed of. If I'd known you as a child, I would've asked to be one of your henchmen.
You know how shy I am. I've always needed someone to drag me out into the open."

page35.text:
"My henchman...?"
...Ah, actually, I bet Sakura would've trained with me daily if we'd known each other as kids.
I can definitely imagine my younger self shouting motivational phrases at her as we ran along the riverbed or meditated in the dojo.

page36.text:
Anyone watching us would have seen us as boss and minion.
Then, Sakura would have grown up big and strong under my guidance,
like this...
...or a devil in girl's clothing like this.

page37.text:
"Urgh..."
I feel a sudden chill.
Thank goodness she turned out so modest and graceful.

page38.text:
"Um, Senpai?"
"Hm? Sorry, just spaced out for a second. Don't mind me, I'm just talking to myself."

page39.text:
"All right, then... But may I ask you a question?"
"Sure. What is it?"

page40.text:
"...I heard from Ms. Fujimura that you were adopted into the Emiya household. Is that true?"
"Hm? Didn't I mention it before? Yeah, Kiritsugu adopted me."

page41.text:
"U-um, Senpai? Is that..."
"It isn't really a secret. It's just what it is. Why do you ask?"

page42.text: "Doesn't it bother you? Being given to a family you don't know, and having to endure a lot of things you didn't like?"

page43.text:
"Ahh, Fuji-nee must have put that idea in your head.
...Well, it might have looked that way during the first year, but I don't think it was that bad, and there wasn't anything I truly disliked."
"S-so, did you enjoy it?"

page44.text:
Hm.
This is the first time anyone's ever asked me that.
After the fire...
My first year with Kiritsugu was a difficult one, spent mostly recovering from my injuries.

page45.text:
After that...
After that, I've just been on the move day after day, like I still am now.
I followed Kiritsugu's footsteps to learn magecraft,
found meaning in helping as many people as I could, and spent my days roaming the town.

page46.text:
Can I truly say I enjoyed it?
I've never had the luxury of considering that question.

page47.text: "Hmm. I'm not sure. I don't know if I can say it was fun. I just wanted to be like my old man."

page48.text:
"You wanted to be a hero, like Ms. Fujimura mentioned?"
Sakura timidly asks.
And I answer,
"Yeah. Is that weird?"
I feel bashful about it, but I say how I really feel.

page49.text:
"No. That isn't wrong. I admire how straightforward you are."
"..."
Her words are calm.
Normally, they'd make me so embarrassed that I couldn't look her in the eye. But the sentiment goes straight to my heart, and I feel like thanking her.

page50.text: "Then, I have another question for you. If I become a bad person, would you forgive me?"

page51.text:
"Huh...?"
I'm taken aback by the sudden question.
But if I consider it seriously...
"No. Sakura, if you do something bad, then I'll be angry. I think I'd be twice as mad as I'd be at anyone else."
I'd probably push everything else from my mind and scold Sakura in that case.

page52.text:
"...Thank goodness. As long as it's you, Senpai."
Sakura nods in apparent relief.

page53.text:
"...?"
Seeing her smile, I feel like this has happened before.

page54.text:
"I'm going back to my room. Good night, Senpai."
Sakura returns to her bedroom.
I watch her leave, and get the odd feeling that I'm forgetting something.

page55.text:
I go back to my bedroom.
I slip into bed quietly to avoid waking Saber, and close my eyes.

page56.text:
"I remember."
Finally, I realize what's been nagging at my mind.
That's right, it was...

page57.text:
It was in the shed back then, too.
Two years ago...no, a year and half, to be exact.

page58.text:
It was two summers ago.
Sakura had come over several times asking to help out around the house, and I'd turned her down each time.
But she wouldn't back down. She showed up here every day, showing more stubbornness than I'd known she had.

page59.text:
Eventually, I gave in. Her tenacity impressed me, and one day, I called her over to the shed to declare my surrender.
"You win, Sakura. So I'm giving you this."
It was an old key.
Kiritsugu used to use it, and it had been put away in the shed for years. I handed it over to Sakura.

page60.text:
Sakura was shocked, and vehemently refused it, saying she didn't deserve to have it.
If memory serves, she insisted that she was too much of a stranger to hold on to even a duplicate of the key.

page61.text:
"Listen, you're not a stranger. You come over and help me every day.
Use this to come and go whenever you want... It would help me out a lot."

page62.text:
I didn't take no for an answer, and pushed it into her hands.
That's when I saw it.
"...Okay. Thank you, Senpai. This is the second time someone important to me has given me something."
Sakura nodded, looking elated.

page63.text:
"Yeah. So that was it."
That's what I was struggling to remember.
Sakura always tries her best, and her smile is always kind and gentle...
But I haven't seen her look this content since that summer day.
